featured_reviews.name: Ratika Arora
featured_reviews.review_text:
If it were possible to rate this place below one star, I absolutely would.
I placed an order on Zomato and made a very simple request—keep the food non-spicy. I didn’t leave it to chance; I clearly mentioned it multiple times in the instructions to avoid any misunderstanding. Despite that, the veg biryani I received was overly spicy and nowhere close to what I had asked for.
The bigger issue, however, was how the restaurant handled it. Instead of acknowledging the mistake, they chose to deny it outright and argue that the dish wasn’t spicy. There was no effort to understand the concern, no apology, and no attempt to fix the situation. When I asked to escalate the matter and speak with the owner, that request was simply refused.
Hoping for a better outcome, I contacted Zomato support—but that turned out to be equally disappointing. The resolution provided was inadequate and unhelpful, which is surprising for a platform that emphasizes customer satisfaction.
What’s most concerning is that this outlet carries a reputed name, yet the experience feels far below standard, almost as if it doesn’t belong to the same brand at all.
To be fair, I’ve visited the Borivali Sky City Mall outlet before, and they deliver exactly what you expect—good food, polite staff, and proper service. Unfortunately, this branch is the complete opposite, showing poor service, lack of professionalism, and no regard for customer requests.
Advice to others: avoid this branch entirely.
It’s not worth the money or the hassle. The entire experience was disappointing, frustrating, and far from acceptable.

featured_reviews.name: Sanjeev Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited 'Shree Balaji - Pure Veg Restaurant' located just a 5-minute walk from my home on a weekday, with my family. The restaurant had a nice interior and was a great place for family outings. However, our dining experience didn't live up to our expectations.

We ordered a variety of dishes, including Veg Manchow soup, All Toppings Pizza, Chinese Draft Sizzler, Mexican Nachos Cheese Ball, French fries and Italian Paneer Tikka with Curd Dip. Unfortunately, the food didn't impress us.

The All Toppings Pizza was just a name that actually had very few toppings and the biggest disappointment was the Mexican Nachos Cheese Ball. It was raw inside and the nachos weren't fresh. We had to return it. The only enjoyable part of the meal was the 300ml glass bottle ThumsUp i had afterward.

In conclusion, despite the pleasant ambiance, the restaurant fell short in terms of taste and quality. The lackluster flavors, especially with the raw cheese ball and underwhelming pizza, left us dissatisfied. Hopefully, the restaurant will work on improving the quality of their dishes to become a better choice for vegetarian cuisine in the neighborhood.

Overall Ratings:
Food: 3/5
Ambiance: 4/5
Service: 4/5
Quantity: 4/5
Value for Money: 3/5

featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Shree Krishna Restaurant, and my experience was nothing short of comforting. Sometimes, all you want is a simple, satisfying Indian meal that feels like home — and that’s exactly what I found here. I ordered Dal Khichdi and Chaas, and it turned out to be the perfect choice for a wholesome, light yet fulfilling lunch.

The Dal Khichdi was cooked to perfection — soft, balanced in spices, and full of that comforting aroma of ghee and dal. It wasn’t too oily or heavy, and every bite felt nourishing and fresh. The texture was just right, neither too thick nor watery, and you could tell it was made with care, not hurriedly thrown together.

The Chaas (buttermilk) complemented it beautifully. It was chilled, perfectly salted, and had that lovely hint of jeera that makes it so refreshing. Together, the khichdi and chaas made for a meal that instantly lifted my mood — simple, traditional, and soul-satisfying.

The restaurant itself has a clean, no-fuss setup with prompt service and polite staff. I really appreciated how quickly the food was served and how humble the overall atmosphere felt. It’s not a fancy dining place, but it’s one of those hidden gems where taste, simplicity, and satisfaction truly stand out.

If you’re craving homely comfort food, I’d highly recommend trying Shree Krishna Restaurant’s Dal Khichdi and Chaas combo — it’s comfort in its purest form!

featured_reviews.name: Deepa Thathagar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, on the last Sunday, my husband and I decided to go out for dinner. We thought of trying a new restaurant nearby.

We chose The Fillo, a recently opened restaurant in Bhayandar West. Excited about visiting the place, and considering it was a weekend, we decided to reach early to avoid waiting. However, our excitement quickly turned into disappointment, resulting in one of the worst dining experiences we’ve ever had.

When we arrived, they informed us that all the tables were occupied and asked us to wait for 30 minutes. We had reached at 7:45 PM, but even after waiting, we didn’t get a table. The host insisted we sit in the garden area, which was vacant. However, we had clearly mentioned that we preferred an AC table and were willing to wait. This made me feel quite awkward—if we had already requested an AC table, why were they trying to force us into the garden area?

To make matters worse, we noticed a group of four people arrive without a reservation, yet they were promptly offered an AC table. When we questioned the host and the manager, they claimed the table was for four people and not for two. My husband and I were furious with this illogical reasoning. After arguing with them, they apologized and eventually arranged a table of six for us.

Once seated, barely 5–7 minutes passed before a staff member approached us and asked us to move to a smaller table for two so they could accommodate another family of 4–5 people. While we agreed to cooperate, we couldn’t help but feel undervalued as customers. Regardless of whether there are two or four diners, everyone is paying for their meal, and this kind of treatment felt discriminatory.

While seated at the table for two, we observed the staff moving another family from a table for six to a table for four, just to accommodate others. The constant shuffling of guests between tables was chaotic and showed a complete lack of management.

The food, unfortunately, didn’t make up for the poor service. The menu was limited, and the dishes we tried were disappointing:

Cheese Fries: Served in a strainer, causing all the liquid cheese to drain off. The fries were dry and lacked flavor. When we complained, they apologized and served cheese separately, but by then, the taste was already ruined.

Chur Chur Naan: This was essentially a crumbled potato paratha with no distinctive flavor or masala.

Pesto Bao: While new and somewhat acceptable, it wasn’t impressive.

Frustrated, we gave up and didn’t order anything else. The overall experience felt like a complete waste of time and money. In hindsight, we should’ve gone to one of our usual dining spots where we’re always satisfied with the meal and service.

I will never recommend The Fillo, even if someone offers to take you there for free or as part of a party.
